proposed.text: Why does moisture content matter when using the NSCP Section 622 machine-graded lumber design-property tables?

options.text: The listed properties apply to dry lumber below 16 percent moisture; green lumber above 28 percent requires reductions, and the middle range may be interpolated.
Moisture content is irrelevant once a piece is machine graded.
Green lumber always receives higher design values than dry lumber.
The checked source requires all machine-graded lumber to be rejected above 16 percent moisture.

rationale.correct: Section 622.2 gives dry-lumber applicability below 16 percent, green-lumber reductions above 28 percent, and interpolation between 16 percent and 28 percent.
rationale.takeaway: Do not apply a machine-graded lumber design value until the moisture range is known.
